thisWeek.label: THIS WEEK
thisWeek.headline: Black Friday is Friday 27 November. Check price histories first.
thisWeek.note: Which? warns that some 'was' prices are misleading, so compare a deal with the last six months of prices on PriceSpy or CamelCamelCamel before you buy.

products.name: Sonos Beam (Gen 2)
products.why: A What Hi-Fi? Award winner for the sixth year in a row, with sound still unbeaten at its price.

products.name: Sony HT-SF150
products.bestFor: A cheap upgrade on TV speakers
products.why: Well built, inexpensive and a clear step up from TV speakers. Dialogue can sound a little muffled.

products.name: Hisense AX5125H
products.bestFor: A full Atmos system on a budget
products.why: Soundbar, subwoofer and two surrounds in one box, with amazing weight, scale and spaciousness for the money. Not quite the calibre of pricier systems.

products.name: Sony Bravia Theatre System 6
products.why: An odd-looking system that stands out in all the right ways. There's no HDMI passthrough, and the cables will put some off.

products.name: Sonos Arc Ultra
products.why: Brilliant with Dolby Atmos soundtracks, with tight, tuneful bass. An award winner for the second year.

products.name: Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2nd Gen)
products.why: Still wonderfully good value, with solid picture and sound. It kept its What Hi-Fi? Award for another year.

products.name: Nanoleaf 4D
products.bestFor: Bias lighting that follows the screen
products.why: A budget alternative to Ambilight that spills your TV's colours onto the wall. The camera needs re-calibrating if you move it.

products.name: Apple TV 4K (2026)
products.why: What Hi-Fi? calls it the best video streamer you can buy, with even better picture and sound. The upgrades are subtle, and BBC iPlayer has no 4K HDR.

products.name: Samsung HW-Q990H
products.why: Soundbar, two surrounds and a sub, improved in detail and scale over its award-winning predecessor. It comfortably won its What Hi-Fi? Awards 2026 category.

products.name: Home Assistant Green
products.why: As easy as Home Assistant gets: setup is simpler than expected and local control feels instant. The dashboard isn't very intuitive for beginners.

products.name: TP-Link Tapo P110M
products.why: A great-value Matter plug that stayed responsive in testing. Energy monitoring works over Matter in Home Assistant and SmartThings, but not Apple Home.

products.name: Philips Hue Essential
products.why: Less than half the price of standard Hue bulbs, and TechRadar saw little colour difference in use. They don't dim as low as regular Hue.

products.name: Nanoleaf Matter Essentials
products.why: Among the most affordable smart lights, with Matter for easy control alongside other brands. No Apple HomeKit without a hub.

products.name: Govee Uplighter Floor Lamp
products.bestFor: A smart corner of the lounge
products.why: Practical task light plus aurora-style effects on the ceiling, with Matter support. It looks a bit bland when off.

products.name: Ezviz EP8 Ultra
products.why: Expert Reviews' best video doorbell overall. No subscription needed, with a chime and spare battery in the box. It's quite bulky.

products.name: TP-Link Tapo D235
products.why: Subscription-free, with a plug-in wireless chime and an enormous battery. Wi-Fi is 2.4GHz only.

products.name: tado Smart Thermostat X
products.bestFor: Smart heating you can fit yourself
products.why: T3's pick for easy installation, and it scales to most heating and hot water setups. Some smart features sit behind a subscription.

products.name: Eufy Omni E25
products.why: Expert Reviews' best robot vacuum overall: a brilliant mopper, fully featured and reasonably priced. The base station is bulky.

products.name: Eufy E20
products.why: A robot vacuum that doubles as a cordless stick, and Expert Reviews' best value pick. No mopping and no anti-tangle brush.

products.name: Philips Hue Twilight
products.why: A realistic sunrise wake-up and wind-down scenes at night. Expensive, even for Hue, and limited without a Hue Bridge.

products.name: Govee Curtain Lights
products.why: TechRadar's smart Christmas lights pick: easy to set up, highly customisable and fine indoors or out. The lights are smaller than they look in promo images.
